description: pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:21-26 (module-level rustdoc) says build_path uses iterative-deepening DFS and guarantees the shortest valid path. The actual implementation since the PathCandidates rewrite is a single-pass DFS at the configured max_depth (with a depth+1 probe to distinguish NoPathFound from DepthExceeded), and PathCandidates' own rustdoc (lib.rs:489-495) explicitly says "No iterative deepening ... Shortest-first is no longer guaranteed". The two docs contradict each other on the same page. Trigger: any caller who reads the crate landing page and relies on the shortest-path guarantee — they will be surprised by a deeper chain returned first in adversarial pools. Fix: rewrite lines 21-26 to describe the single-pass DFS + depth probe behavior, or delete the # Algorithm section and defer to build_path / PathCandidates rustdoc which already describe it correctly.
title: module-level doc lies: "iterative-deepening DFS" + "shortest valid path" guarantee no longer true
